subject: Linguistics
title: Presupposition
description: A micro-lesson that makes Presupposition usable.

hook.text: 'The king of France is bald.' Wait—France has no king. Is the sentence true, false, or neither?

buildup.text: Presuppositions are background assumptions a sentence takes for granted.

discovery.text: 'Stop smoking' presupposes you smoke; 'his car' presupposes he has one.

twist.text: Unlike entailments, presuppositions survive negation: 'He didn't stop smoking' still implies he smoked.

climax.text: Presupposition failure creates confusion—the listener's background assumption doesn't hold.

punchline.text: Half the meaning hides in what's already assumed.

quiz.question: How do presuppositions behave under negation?
